quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 and full-year 2025 results (prepared remarks, Tony Balow): 2025 was MPS's fourteenth consecutive year of growth with full-year revenue of $2.8 billion, up 26.4% from 2024; Q4 2025 was a record quarterly revenue of $751.2 million, 1.9% above Q3 2025 and 20.8% higher than 2024. Non-enterprise data end markets grew by over 40% year-over-year. CFO Bernie Blegen added that enterprise data, previously the largest revenue end market, 'Had actually declined 2%' in 2025 while the company grew 26%. The call also announced Bernie Blegen's retirement as CFO, with corporate controller Rob Dean as interim CFO.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 2025 record revenue $751.2 million (1.9% above Q3 2025, 20.8% higher than 2024); 2025 revenue $2.8 billion (up 26.4%); non-enterprise data end markets grew by over 40%; enterprise data declined 2% in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Ordering and backlog turned up in Q4 2025: management 'saw a good step up in the ordering patterns', the book-to-bill ratio 'was well in excess of one', and backlog is 'starting to extend out into Q2 2026'; channel inventory stayed at the low end of MPS's range. Bernie Blegen: after a period of very short lead times, MPS is now 'seeing longer ordering patterns because some of our customers are concerned about capacity constraints. Not necessarily with us, but just in general.' He called 'the first half for enterprise data in particular, but for the company, is more secure', with the second half still uncertain, and flagged the need to sort 'real demand' from possible 'double ordering on the part of our customers as they try to secure capacity.' Management expects strength in enterprise data, communications and automotive to extend into Q1 and the rest of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill well in excess of one; backlog extending into Q2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Enterprise-data (AI/server power) outlook for 2026 raised on Q4 ordering: Tony Balow said last quarter he talked about 'a range of between 30-40%' and 'maybe I can increase that to a floor of 50% growth' (the transcript prints 'for 2025'; the question was about the 2026 outlook). CEO Michael Hsing said 'I thought that we can do a lot more than that, conservatively', citing design wins 'across the board, not from one company' at multiple very big customers, calling MPS 'one of the valuable AI power supplies', and saying MPS has the capacity to deliver this year. Drivers named: growing existing customers, adding new customers, new platforms coming to market and server tailwinds; strong data center demand is also pulling through storage, optical modules and switches. On CPU vs GPU, 'the lines between AI, GPUs, and CPU are getting pretty blurry' as they use the same kind of power supply, and MPS is trending well in both. Bernie Blegen: MPS is engaged strategically with the 'top six, seven customers', developing the next generation and 'the one beyond that', plus a long tail of mid and small customers.
quarterly_data.figure: enterprise data 2026 growth floor 50% (from a 30-40% range last quarter)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: MPS achieved its milestone of securing more than $4 billion of geographically balanced capacity in 2025 and continues to add supply chain partners. Management said 'we don't have constraints on our capacity side.' Asked about the next three years, Michael Hsing said MPS established a supply management organization at the beginning of last year covering not only silicon but also silicon carbide, gallium nitride materials and module components, with suppliers going through heavy audits; 'We're expanding very fast.'
quarterly_data.figure: more than $4 billion of geographically balanced capacity secured

quarterly_data.signal: 800V data-center power: in 2025 MPS positioned for a further shift to solutions by sampling its 800-volt power solution for data centers. Asked whether 800-volt racks will use GaN or silicon carbide, Michael Hsing said MPS is developing silicon carbide and in the last few years developed its own GaN devices (he mentioned '100 volts'); 'that revenue is not for this year, not for even for next year. So, okay, maybe end of the next year. However, we're the first company to sample it.' Tony Balow: whether GaN or silicon carbide is what is demanded, MPS expects to be well-positioned.
quarterly_data.figure: 800-volt power solution sampling; revenue 'maybe end of the next year'

quarterly_data.signal: Modules and vertical power: MPS had record module revenue in 2025 and is migrating 'from silicon to systems', with customers changing from silicon to modules on MPS's power density. On the packaging innovation to double module current density (raised by an analyst), Michael Hsing said 'We start to sampling those products' and 'expect to have a shipping in this quarter and next quarter', with customers having gone through qualification. On vertical power delivery: 'everybody is going to a vertical power'; Bernie Blegen called it 'the only energy-efficient solution' at high current. On server CPUs, the majority still use 12 volts while some models use 48 volts, and modules are 'the way to go'. Michael Hsing also said MPS is moving into MCUs, data converters and high-speed products.
quarterly_data.figure: record module revenue in 2025; higher-density modules shipping this quarter and next quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnect power (optical modules / CPO): Tony Balow said MPS has seen great growth in optical modules over the past year and a half and treats the market as 'interconnect', with engagements for CPO and active copper as well; 'we would expect optical module to continue to grow as you start to see the 1.6 ramp', and communications should be a growth area in 2026 on both optical modules and data center switches. On co-packaged optics, Michael Hsing said higher current and higher density is 'always good for us'; Tony Balow added 'I don't think that necessarily moves the needle on 26', but MPS is engaged over the longer term.
quarterly_data.figure: optical module growth expected with the 1.6 ramp; CPO not a 2026 revenue driver

quarterly_data.signal: Memory and storage power: MPS had very little DDR4 business, but its DDR5 business is ramping as memory shifts to DDR5 ('we clearly see the volumes now', last year and this year), and MPS is expanding product lines inside memory modules. The SSD/HDD part of storage also saw an uptick, 'Being pulled through much more by the enterprise than consumer', so management describes storage as data-center driven.

Gross margin: the corporate model is 55-60%, and MPS has been trending between 55.5 and 55.8 over the last four to six quarters, the low end of the model (Bernie Blegen). With backlog now developing, MPS expects to resume at some time during the year its historical cadence of incremental sequential improvements of 'maybe 10 to 20 basis points quarter over quarter.'
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin model 55-60%; trending between 55.5 and 55.8; expected improvement of 10 to 20 basis points quarter over quarter
